chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever gives a believer a drink of water from wherever he is able to provide water, Allah will give him, for each drink, seventy thousand good deeds; and if he gives him from where he is not able to provide water, it is as if he has freed ten necks from the children of Ismail.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for giving water to a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the spiritual merit of providing water to a believer, distinguishing between accessible and scarce sources to highlight the value of effort and sacrifice. The comparison to freeing ten slaves from the progeny of Ismail emphasizes the high status of this act within Shia tradition, linking physical sustenance to spiritual liberation. This reward structure reflects the broader Islamic principle that ease in giving yields consistent merit, while difficulty amplifies it significantly.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who quenches a Momin with a drink of water from wherever he is able upon the water, Allahazwj would Give him, with each drink, seventy thousand good deeds; and if he were to quench him from where he has no ability upon the water, so it is as if he as freed ten necks from the children of Ismailas’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever serves a drink of water to a believer who (himself) also can find water, Allah will give him seventy thousand good deeds for each drink and if he provides a drink of water when he (himself) is not able to find one it will be like setting free ten persons from the descendents of Tsma’il.’”
